text:
jamal: quick heads-up — noticed a p95 latency jump on the model-mix route after the continuous-batcher tweak landed on canary. digging in now

eva: ugh, saw alert too. is this when fallback to quantized variants happens?

jamal: looks correlated. trace shows an increase in fragmented batches when requests hit compat-set boundaries and then fallback triggers a different kernel family (cuBLAS vs custom fused)

rachel: can you paste profile snapshot? even a small flame or hot functions helps.

jamal: attaching quick profiler excerpt:
```
Batcher: form_batch (ms): mean=2.7 p95=18.4 -> after tweak p95=42.9
Kernel selection: select_kernel_for_variant: avg=0.6ms, spike to 9ms on fallback
KV cache hitrate: 0.78 -> 0.62 when variant switching increases
Fragmentation ratio: 0.18 -> 0.37
```

mike: that kernel selection spike is concerning — if batcher groups incompatible variants then select_kernel has to do extra checks and sometimes fall back to safe kernels which are slower. also KV cache thrash will increase token costs

nora: do we have a reproducible test? small load generator that mixes variants by weight?

jamal: yes, replayed in staging: 60% modelA (FP16 fast kernels), 40% modelB (int8 quantized). With the new permissive merge window=5ms batches cohabitate more and then fallback occurs mid-batch. results:
 - throughput (tokens/s) -6.8%
 - p95 latency +88%
 - token-cost +12%

perf-bot: canary report: https://perf.dashboard/canary/1978880000 (summary attached) :rotating_light:

eva: idea: make compat-set matching stricter for the first N ms of request lifetime (batch-stickiness) so we avoid mid-batch variant churn. or make select_kernel cheaper (cache decisions)

rachel: agreed. also consider token_budget per-queue so very long requests don't hold batches and force mixing of short quant requests

mike: propose quick config to try on canary:
```yaml
queue_policy:
  token_budget_per_batch: 96
  permissive_merge_ms: 3  # shrink merge window
  variant_stickiness_ttl_ms: 60000  # keep same-variant preference for 60s
  allow_merge_on_kernel_match_only: true
```

nora: small tweak, push canary, run the staged mix generator for 30m and collect kv-hit, batch-size distribution, kernel-switch counts

jamal: started a canary with those settings now. infra-bot will post results

infra-bot: canary started: id=ci-197888-02, config=queue_policy/variant-stickiness, start=1978880060

perf-bot: initial 10m snapshot: fragmentation ratio down to 0.12, KV hitrate back to 0.76, p95 back to baseline +8% (from +88%). continuing run

eva: great. note we still see some workload corners where fallback unavoidable (mixed sequence lengths + token budgets). we should also consider kernel selection memoization keyed by (model_variant, seq_len_bucket, device_family) to avoid repeated heavy decisions

rachel: agree — add cheap cache with TTL 30s for kernel choice. also a small optimization: fast-path when all pending slots in batch share identical model/quant flags

mike: can someone update the docs for the queue policies? small table of tradeoffs would help SREs tune for mixed-variant traffic

jamal: will write a short runbook and put it under eng-runtime/runbooks/batching.md. will include metrics to watch: fragmentation_ratio, kv_hitrate, kernel_switch_count, p95_latency, tokens_per_sec

nora: also flag to product: recommend customer-facing guidance when mixing quantized & fp variants in same route — maybe encourage variant routing by prefix or sticky routing for steady-state sessions

jamal: thanks all — will keep canary running for an hour and post final numbers. next steps: 1) try kernel memo TTL 30s, 2) add batch-stickiness opt-in per-route, 3) doc + runbook 4) consider telemetry alert for kernel_switch_count rising > 5%

perf-bot: canary final (60m): throughput -0.9%, p95 +6%, token-cost +1.2%, fragmentation 0.11, kv-hitrate 0.75. marking as improved vs baseline canary regression

eva: nice job. opening follow-up PRs for kernel memo and runbook

jamal: PRs: #3481 (kernel memo cache), #3482 (queue policy tunables), #3483 (runbook). will schedule a short sync tomorrow to pick priority

mike: add a small regression test in perf-harness that mixes variants and asserts fragmentation < 0.2 and kernel_switch_count < 3 per minute

rachel: noted. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
